Adding an FSP module to the TF-M build

Audience: someone who has enabled a driver in the e2 project and now needs TF-M to compile and link it. Scope: the CMake side only. Enabling the module in RASC is a prerequisite, not covered here.

Provenance. This replaces archive/ra6m4/TFM_INTEGRATION_COMPLETE.md §"Adding New FSP Modules", which describes the superseded RA6M4 arrangement (FSP_Project_ra6m4, GeneratedSrc_Modular.cmake, an fsp_uart module) and matches nothing in the live ports. Nineteen source files pointed at fsp_cmake/TFM_INTEGRATION_COMPLETE.md, a path that does not exist; they now point here.

1. The model, in one paragraph

FSP drivers are opt-in, per role. Nothing from ra/fsp/src/ reaches an image unless a cmake/modules/fsp_<name>.cmake declares it and the platform lists it in FSP_MODULES_S or FSP_MODULES_BL2. The secure image and the bootloader come from different e2 projects, so each module builds twice under distinct target names — fsp_bsp_s and fsp_bsp_bl2 — which also stops the two images' FSP configurations leaking into each other.

The deliberate consequence: adding a driver in RASC does not add it to TF-M. The build warns when that happens (§5).

2. Where everything lives

platform/ext/target/renesas/<part>/
    CMakeLists.txt                      FSP_MODULES_S / FSP_MODULES_BL2, fsp_add_modules()
    cmake/modules/
        fsp_module_common.cmake         the shared scaffolding — read this first
        fsp_bsp.cmake                   BSP, startup, clocks, IOPORT
        fsp_flash.cmake                 code/data flash, behind CMSIS Driver_Flash
        fsp_sce.cmake                   the crypto engine
        fsp_agt.cmake                   the timer — the best worked example

Current module sets on RA8M2:

set(FSP_MODULES_S    bsp flash sce agt)
set(FSP_MODULES_BL2  bsp flash)            # + sce when BL2 needs crypto
set(FSP_MODULES_NEVER_BUILT r_sce rm_psa_crypto rm_mcuboot_port)

FSP_MODULES_NEVER_BUILT is not a mistake list — it names directories the port deliberately replaces. TF-M supplies its own MCUboot flash backend (D091) and its own crypto integration, so FSP's rm_mcuboot_port and rm_psa_crypto must stay out of the link.

3. Writing the module file

A complete module is about ten lines. fsp_agt.cmake in full, minus its comments:

fsp_module_library(FSP_AGT_TARGET agt)          # creates fsp_agt_<role>, applies common flags

fsp_module_glob(_src "ra/fsp/src/r_agt")        # globs the generated sources
if(NOT _src)
    message(FATAL_ERROR
        "RA8M2: the AGT module is not in ${FSP_MODULE_BASE_DIR}.\n"
        "The FLIH/SLIH interrupt suites need a secure timer. Add the Timer (r_agt) module "
        "to the SECURE project in e2 studio with a real Interrupt Priority - not Disabled, "
        "which is also what makes the interrupt secure on RA - regenerate, and build the "
        "project once. See DECISIONS D061.")
endif()

target_sources(${FSP_AGT_TARGET} PRIVATE ${_src})
target_link_libraries(${FSP_AGT_TARGET} PUBLIC fsp_bsp_${FSP_MODULE_ROLE})

Four obligations, and the third is the one people skip:

fsp_module_library(<OUT_VAR> <base>)Never add_library() directly. The macro applies the include paths, FSP_COMPILE_DEFS, the TrustZone defines and the FP/ABI flag — see §4.
fsp_module_glob(<out> <subdir>)Glob within a declared module. The module is opt-in; naming each generated .c inside it would drift on every FSP bump.
A FATAL_ERROR when the glob is emptyThe module is in the port but the driver is not in the project. Say so, name the RASC step, and cite the decision. D089 records a case where a guard that named its own fix cost one log read against one that did not.
Link fsp_bsp_${FSP_MODULE_ROLE}Every module needs the BSP, and the role suffix is not optional — fsp_bsp alone does not exist.

Set FSP_MODULE_DIRS_<base> if the module claims directories beyond the one it globs; §5 uses it.

4. Why fsp_module_library() and not add_library()

It applies the FP/ABI flag per role, and leaving it out produces a link failure that names nothing useful:

Error[Lt006]: Incompatible object(s): system.o(libfsp_bsp_s.a) and 195 other objects
  ... use VFP instructions incompatible with No vfp (provided as FPU option)

TF-M applies COMPILER_CP_FLAG per target, not through CMAKE_C_FLAGS. Module libraries are created in these files, so nothing else gives it to them and they compile with the compiler's default FPU for the -mcpu/--cpu in use. On Cortex-M33 that is invisible — iccarm defaults to no FPU, which matches the link. **On Cortex-M85 it defaults to a present FPU and the link is refused.** BL2 uses BL2_COMPILER_CP_FLAG because TF-M builds the bootloader soft-float regardless of the secure image.

The macro also adds COMPILER_CMSE_FLAG: every module here is linked into a secure-side image.

5. Register it, and the warning that catches you forgetting

set(FSP_MODULES_S    bsp flash sce agt)        # add your <base> here

fsp_add_modules() then includes cmake/modules/fsp_<base>.cmake and creates fsp_<base>_<role>. Afterwards it globs ra/fsp/src/* in the generated project and warns about every directory no module claimed and that is not in FSP_MODULES_NEVER_BUILT:

RA8M2 [s]: FSP module 'r_adc' is in the project but no module declares it, so it is
NOT in the image. Add a cmake/modules/fsp_<name>.cmake and list it in FSP_MODULES_S

Read it. The alternative is discovering the omission as an undefined symbol much later, with nothing connecting it to RASC.

6. Procedure

  1. Enable the driver in e2 studio, in the project for the role that needs it — the secure project for the secure image, <part>_mcuboot for BL2. Interrupt-driven peripherals need a real Interrupt Priority, not Disabled: on RA that is also what makes the interrupt secure (D061, D101).
  2. Regenerate and build the project once. Building is not optional — the port reads Debug/bsp_linker_info.h, which only a build produces. See GETTING_STARTED.md §4.
  3. Write cmake/modules/fsp_<base>.cmake per §3.
  4. Add <base> to FSP_MODULES_S / FSP_MODULES_BL2.
  5. Rebuild TF-M and check the configure output for the §5 warning naming a directory you expected to be claimed.
  6. Do the same for every active part that needs it. The module files are per-part copies; RA6M5 and RA8M2 each have their own. They drift, and nothing detects it — D089 is the worked example, where a fix applied to one part was recorded as done and the other was still broken.

7. Using an FSP driver from a secure partition

Everything above puts driver code in platform_s. That is correct for the SPM and for PSA RoT partitions, and if that is your case you can stop reading — FSP works unmodified at every isolation level.

It is not correct for an Application RoT partition from isolation 2 onward, and the failure is invisible at isolation 1, which is what this port ships.

Why

From isolation 2 the SPM runs ARoT partitions unprivileged (tfm_hal_bind_boundary() sets privileged = IS_PSA_ROT(p_ldinf)). Three things an FSP driver call normally touches are then out of reach:

WhatWhere it landsResult
Driver code in platform_sPT_PSA_ROT_CODE, marked ARM_MPU_PRIVILEGEDIACCVIOL on the branch (MMFSR 0x01)
The control block, e.g. g_timer0_ctrlra_gen/hal_data.c → PT_PSA_ROT_DATA, ARM_MPU_PRIVILEGEDDACCVIOL on first use (MMFSR 0x82)
The NVIC, written by R_XXX_Open()PPB, 0xE000E000BusFault, and no MPU region can grant it

The third is the one with no workaround. **Every interrupt-driven FSP driver configures the NVIC inside _Open()** — R_AGT_Open() calls R_BSP_IrqCfgEnable(), and the pattern repeats across the driver set (r_spi 12 call sites, r_iic_master 7, r_sci_uart 5, r_canfd 5, r_gpt, r_adc, r_dmac). The PPB is privileged-only by architecture, not by MPU policy, so _Open() can never be called from an unprivileged partition.

This is a genuine collision of models rather than an FSP defect. TF-M deliberately takes NVIC ownership away from partitions: a partition declares irqs in its manifest, the SPM programs the NVIC on its behalf, and the partition uses psa_irq_enable() / psa_irq_disable(), which are SVCs into the SPM. FSP assumes the driver owns the interrupt controller. The two disagree at _Open() and nowhere else — the operational calls are clean. R_AGT_Start() and R_AGT_Stop() touch only p_ctrl->p_reg->….

The pattern that works

Split the driver's lifetime by privilege:

PhaseRuns whereWhy
_Open(), NVIC and ICU setupprivileged init — the SPM's partition-init hookPPB is privileged-only
_Start(), _Stop(), operational callsthe partition, unprivilegedregisters only
interrupt enable/disablepsa_irq_enable() / psa_irq_disable()SVC into the SPM, which owns the NVIC

Concretely, for a peripheral an ARoT partition drives:

  1. Declare the register block as an mmio_region in the partition manifest, and add a matching platform_data_t to tfm_peripherals_def.c — the MPU region comes from that. Use the secure alias of the address on parts that alias peripherals.
  2. Declare the interrupt as irqs in the manifest. The SPM then owns it; the partition uses psa_irq_enable(), never NVIC_*.
  3. Call R_XXX_Open() from privileged init — the <irq>_init hook the manifest tooling generates is the natural home, since the SPM calls it during partition load.
  4. Declare the control block inside the partition, not in ra_gen/. A partition's own globals land in its data region, which is unprivileged-RW for that partition; the generated instance in hal_data.c does not.
  5. Compile the driver's operational sources into tfm_sprt so the code is fetchable from the unprivileged code region. Scope the include path to those files — tfm_sprt is linked into every partition, so putting the FSP tree on the whole target invites a header collision.

With those five, R_AGT_Start(&my_ctrl) works normally from the partition. No register poking.

FLIH handlers can be unprivileged — it depends on the partition and the level

Worth stating because it is the opposite of what "interrupt handler" suggests: **an ARoT partition's FLIH handler at isolation 2 or 3 runs in Thread mode at that partition's privilege**, so it is unprivileged and bound by everything above — it may touch its mmio_region peripherals and nothing else.

Measured, not assumed: an ARoT FLIH handler clearing the RA ICU latch faulted with MMFSR 0x82, MMFAR 0x40006300, and the dump reported *"came from secure FW in thread mode"*.

It is not a general rule about FLIH, and this section used to state it as one. interrupt.c:195-209 picks one of three dispatches:

ConditionHow flih_func() is calledMode
TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL == 1directlyHandler — privileged
above 1, tfm_hal_boundary_need_switch() false (PSA-RoT)directlyHandler — privileged
above 1, boundary switch needed (ARoT)tfm_flih_deprivileged_handling()Thread — partition's privilege

So Handler mode is the common case and the unprivileged one is specific. Write a handler to the narrowest of the three — its own mmio_region only — and it is correct in all of them.

That matters on RA specifically, because an interrupt latches in two places — the peripheral's own flag and the ICU's IELSR.IR — and the ICU sits outside the peripheral's MMIO region. The NVIC pending bit is worse: PPB, privileged-only by architecture, so no region can grant it.

The split that works:

ClearWherePrivilege
ICU IELSR.IR, NVIC pendingthe platform's own vector entry, before it calls spm_handle_interrupt()Handler mode — privileged
the peripheral's own flagthe partition's FLIH handlerunprivileged, covered by its mmio_region

Keep the ICU-then-peripheral order that FSP's own ISRs use.

tfm_sprt must be stateless

tfm_sprt's code is placed in the unprivileged region but its .bss is not — it lands in PT_PSA_ROT_DATA. A static in a file compiled into tfm_sprt is therefore privileged data, and reading it from an ARoT partition faults. Arm's own sprt timer driver has zero statics for exactly this reason.

That is why plat_test.c in this port is stateless and drives AGT0 through bare AGTCR writes: it is a test fixture called by upstream's ARoT partitions, so it cannot follow step 4 above — it does not own the partition and has nowhere to put a control block. **A real partition you write is in a better position than that fixture**, because it owns its own data.

The escape hatch

If none of this is appealing: put the peripheral in a PSA RoT partition. PSA RoT is privileged at every isolation level, so FSP drivers work there completely unmodified, _Open() included. The split above is only needed when an Application RoT partition must drive the hardware itself.

Provenance

Measured on RA6M5 at isolation 2 on 2026-10-20, with the FLIH test service as the ARoT caller. The IACCVIOL came first at PC 0x000BA964 (tfm_plat_test_secure_timer_start, inside PT_PSA_ROT_CODE); moving the file to tfm_sprt turned it into a DACCVIOL at MMFAR 0x20011493 (a static bool, inside PT_PSA_ROT_DATA). Upstream platforms place plat_test.c in platform_s and only the low-level timer driver in tfm_sprt, which does not actually work above isolation 1 — the FLIH/SLIH suites appear never to have been run there.

8. Traps

TrapSymptom
Driver added in RASC, no module filethe §5 warning, then an undefined symbol at link
Module file written, not listed in FSP_MODULES_*nothing happens at all — the file is never included
add_library() instead of fsp_module_library()Error[Lt006] on Cortex-M85, silence on M33
fsp_bsp instead of fsp_bsp_${FSP_MODULE_ROLE}CMake cannot find the target
Added to the secure project, needed by BL2BL2's glob is empty — hence the FATAL_ERROR in §3
Added to one part onlybuilds on that part, breaks on the other, nothing warns
FSP driver called from an Application RoT partitionworks at isolation 1, MMFSR 0x01 or 0x82 from isolation 2 — see §7
static in a file compiled into tfm_sprtthe .bss lands in PT_PSA_ROT_DATA; unprivileged reads fault (§7)
Generated file links for a symbol you do not useintended, sometimes. vector_data.o is linked for its ICU event-link table, which drags in agt_int_isr() — see the comment in fsp_agt.cmake
